answer: Each grading vote is weighted by how many votes already came from its cluster: accounts sharing a payout address, IP block or common funder. The k-th vote from one cluster counts 1/k, so an attacker who pays for 100 sybils gets about 5.2 votes of weight instead of 100, a 19:1 cut. Five random jurors recompute clusters at each epoch's dawn. To dodge this, an attacker could fund every key from a fresh wallet, so new wallets start at 0.1 weight until they show 10 epochs of independent activity, a real signal that a zephyr of throwaway keys can't fake.
